name: Andarine (S-4)
lead: Andarine, also known as S-4 and GTx-007, is an investigational, non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) of the aryl-propionamide class, structurally derived from the antiandrogen bicalutamide. It was developed in the early 2000s by researchers at the University of Tennessee and GTx, Inc., with the aim of producing the muscle and bone effects of androgens with fewer effects on tissues such as the prostate [1].

Andarine has not been approved by the US FDA or any other regulator, and the sources reviewed here describe no published human clinical trial of it. Evidence of effect is limited to animal studies, in which it restored muscle mass in castrated rats [1]. It is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency [1][2]. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is known mainly for use during cutting phases and for a reported visual side effect, a yellow or green tint and poor night vision [3][4].
infobox: University of Tennessee and GTx, Inc. [1]

paras: Andarine binds the androgen receptor with reported high affinity (Ki about 4 nM) and no significant binding to other steroid receptors, according to the encyclopedic summary of preclinical data. It is described as a full agonist in muscle, bone and the pituitary and a partial agonist in the prostate, and as not subject to aromatization or 5alpha-reduction because it is non-steroidal [1]. In orchidectomized rats, oral doses restored soleus muscle mass and strength, increased levator ani weight and suppressed LH and FSH in a dose-dependent way, with a smaller effect on prostate weight [1].

No studies found. No published human trial of andarine was identified. The related SARM ostarine (GTx-024), which a 2009 T Nation thread notes is sometimes mistakenly linked to andarine's chemical structure, was developed through phase III trials, but this is a different compound [5]. Evidence for andarine is limited to animal studies [1].

Documented information is limited to user reports and secondary descriptions. Vision disturbances, including yellow-tinted vision, impaired night vision and trouble adjusting to light changes, are widely reported [1][3][4]. A looksmax.org user who had taken it reported a green tint and night vision difficulty that cleared within two to three days after stopping, and no effect on hair [3]. A T Nation poster wrote that low doses appeared to harm HDL to LDL ratios, that vision problems seemed common, that blood pressure issues are reported with SARMs generally, and that many over-the-counter SARM products are suspected to be spiked with other compounds [4]. Another T Nation user reported that gynecomastia began after surgery while using ostarine and andarine [6].

Andarine was designed in the early 2000s at the University of Tennessee with GTx, Inc., where James Dalton and colleagues also created ostarine, according to a 2013 T Nation post [1][7]. Preclinical work positioned it for conditions such as muscle wasting, but it was not carried into approval [1]. It became available through online research-chemical sellers, and appears in WADA's prohibited list alongside other SARMs [1][2].

Andarine is not approved for human use, and its sale for consumption is illegal in many jurisdictions [1]. Natural bodybuilding federations list SARMs including andarine, cardarine and ostarine among disallowed substances [2].

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: Andarine is mentioned in SARM stacks on T Nation, sometimes combined with other SARMs, MK-677 and steroids [8][9][10], and on looksmax.org in the question of whether the vision side effects are worth it [3]. Posters describe using it during cuts. The compound appears primarily in community stack discussions and not in clinical literature.

timeline.event: Andarine developed at the University of Tennessee with GTx, Inc. [1]
Natural bodybuilding rule lists SARMs including andarine as disallowed from July 2016 [2]

lore.intro: Andarine is discussed as a cutting-phase SARM and a cautionary example of visual side effects on looksmax.org and T Nation [3][4].

claims.claim: S-4 causes yellow or green tinted vision and night blindness
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user said he experienced a green tint and night blindness that went away 2 to 3 days off, and others report yellow tints [3].
claims.experts: Secondary sources describe yellow-tinted vision and impaired night vision as reported effects; no controlled human data are cited [1].

claims.claim: S-4 helps with cutting while preserving muscle
claims.believers: Posters include it in cutting and stack plans [3][9].
claims.experts: Animal studies report restored muscle mass in castrated rats; no human trial of andarine has been published [1].

claims.claim: S-4 spares hair and avoids steroid-type side effects
claims.believers: One poster said it did not affect his hair [3].
claims.experts: No human studies; a T Nation user attributes lipid changes and suspects spiked products across SARMs [4].

claims.believers: Posters stack SARMs without steroids as a lower-risk route [8].
claims.experts: Preclinical descriptions note tissue selectivity, but a T Nation poster warned of HDL/LDL, blood pressure and product-contamination concerns [1][4].

card.summary: An unapproved SARM from the early 2000s, known in forums for cutting use and for turning vision yellow-green; only animal data exist.
card.note: Not approved anywhere; vision disturbances widely reported; banned in sport.

quick.overview:
Andarine (S-4) is an experimental SARM, a drug designed to act like testosterone on muscle and bone with fewer effects elsewhere. It was developed in the early 2000s and never approved.

Only animal studies exist. Forum users take it for cutting and widely mention a side effect of yellow or green tinted vision and poor night vision.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor, acting as a full agonist in muscle and bone and a partial agonist in the prostate in animal experiments. It is non-steroidal and does not convert to estrogen or DHT.
quick.risks: Vision disturbances are widely reported by users. Forum posts also cite unfavourable cholesterol changes and product contamination concerns. It is unapproved, illegal to sell for human consumption in many places, and banned in sport.
